Welcome to the support page for EveryHour, the hours tracker and pay stub checker for hourly workers in the United States.
App: EveryHour — Hours Tracker (hours tracking and pay stub checking for hourly workers in the United States)
App: EveryHour — Hours Tracker

Welcome to the support page for EveryHour, the hours tracker and pay stub checker for hourly workers in the United States. If you experience any issues, have questions, or want to provide feedback, please contact us using the information below.

Email: vincenttrandeveloper@gmail.com You can also send a bug report, feedback, or a feature suggestion directly from the app — open Settings → Send feedback. Reports sent this way include your app version and platform, which helps us diagnose issues faster. Please do not attach pay stubs or other personal documents to a report. We aim to respond as quickly as possible.

Clocking in and out, editing shifts, and recording breaks Jobs, pay rates, and the state and city used for wage rules Reading a pay stub with the camera and confirming the numbers Wage reports (PDF), spreadsheets (CSV), and ZIP exports Encrypted backups and restoring onto a new phone Reminders — forgot to clock out, payday, backup, end of a pay period App lock with Face ID, fingerprint, or passcode Subscription, purchase, or restore questions

EveryHour keeps every shift, break, and edit on your phone. Every change to a shift is saved as a new entry with the reason you give, so your records keep their history and are harder to dispute later. If a clock-out is missing, open the shift and add the end time — the app will ask for a reason and keep both versions. To make the timing of a record harder to challenge, leave Settings → "Check the time online" on. The app then reads the current time from a web server instead of trusting the phone clock alone. Pay rates, overtime, and premium rules come from the state and city set on the job — check them in Settings → Jobs if an amount looks wrong.

Photograph the stub and the app reads the text with your phone's own text recognition (Apple Vision on iPhone, Google ML Kit on Android). The photo never leaves your device. Good light and a flat, uncreased stub make a large difference to accuracy. Always review the numbers the app extracted before confirming them — you can correct any field by hand. Any comparison the app makes between a stub and your records is an estimate from the figures you confirmed, not a legal determination.

A wage report (PDF), a spreadsheet (CSV), a ZIP file, or an encrypted backup is created on your phone and leaves it only when you send it somewhere yourself through the share sheet. Each report records the version of the wage rules used and when they were last checked. Backups are encrypted with a password you choose. We never see that password and cannot recover it — if it is lost, the backup cannot be opened. Keep a backup somewhere outside the phone if your records matter to you.

EveryHour offers optional paid plans — monthly, yearly, and a one-time lifetime purchase. There are no free trials. Purchases are handled entirely by Apple or Google. To restore a purchase on a new device or after reinstalling, open Settings → Restore Purchases while signed in to the same Apple Account or Google account used for the original purchase. For billing issues, cancellations, or refunds, use the store's own subscription management: iOS: Settings → [Your Name] → Subscriptions Android: Play Store → Profile → Payments & subscriptions → Subscriptions If Pro ends, your hours, pay stubs, and exported files stay on your phone and remain readable.

EveryHour stores your shifts, pay stubs, notes, and reports only on your device — there is no cloud sync and we hold no copy. Deleting the app, or using Settings → Delete all data, removes everything permanently, and we cannot restore it for you. If you want a copy kept somewhere else, create an encrypted backup or export your records, then save the file to Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive, or wherever you prefer.

Before contacting support, please try: Restarting the app Updating to the latest app version Restarting your device Reinstalling the app if necessary — note that this erases your local records unless you have exported them or made a backup first

EveryHour is built so that your work records stay on your phone. There is no account and no sign-up. No email, no password, no social login. Your hours, breaks, pay rates, workplaces, pay stub photos, notes, and reports stay on your phone and are not sent to us. Pay stub photos are read on your phone. They are never uploaded. No ads, no ad SDKs, no tracking across other apps or websites. We never sell your personal information. What does leave the device: a request to a web server to check the current time, anonymous usage statistics, crash reports, purchase/entitlement events — and, only if you choose to send one, the content of a feedback report. None of these contain your hours or your pay. The rest of this policy explains each of those points precisely.

This policy applies to the EveryHour app distributed on the Apple App Store and Google Play, and to any future updates, to the extent that the features described are actually enabled on your device. It does not cover Apple's or Google's own processing of your data as the platform and store operator, or the processing done by any service you choose to send an exported file to (email, Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive), which is governed by their own privacy policies.

Everything you enter or create in EveryHour is stored in the app's private storage on your device. None of it is transmitted to us, and none of it is transmitted to any third party as part of normal use of the app: Shifts, clock-in and clock-out times, and breaks Jobs, employers, pay rates, and the state and city you choose for wage rules Pay stub photos and the numbers read from them Notes, letters you mark as sent, and the edit history of each record Reports (PDF), spreadsheets (CSV), ZIP files, and encrypted backups you export We cannot see any of it and we do not have a copy. Text recognition. When you photograph a pay stub, the text is read by your phone's own text recognition — Apple Vision on iPhone, Google ML Kit bundled inside the app on Android. The photo and the text read from it do not leave your phone. Location. If you tap "Use my location" while setting up a workplace, the app reads your position once to suggest the state and city whose wage rules apply. The coordinates are compared with maps built into the app; they are not stored and not sent anywhere. You can choose the place by hand instead, and the app works fully without ever granting location access. Exports and backups. A wage report, spreadsheet, ZIP file, or encrypted backup is created on your phone and only leaves it when you send it somewhere yourself, using your phone's share sheet. Backups are encrypted with a password you choose; we never see the password and cannot recover it. App lock. Face ID, Touch ID, fingerprint, or passcode checks are performed by your phone's operating system. EveryHour only learns whether the check passed — it never receives your biometric data. Reminders. Notifications (forgot to clock out, payday, backup, an approaching pay period date) are scheduled locally on your phone. No push service is used and no notification content is sent through a server.
documents.s: 2. Data that stays on your device

documents.t: To make your records harder to dispute, the app asks a web server for the current time — it reads the date header of a response from firebasestorage.googleapis.com or www.google.com. The request contains nothing about you or your records; the server sees only the standard request metadata, including your IP address. You can turn this off in Settings → "Check the time online".

The app records which features are used — for example that a report was exported or a paywall was shown — together with a random identifier for the app installation and standard technical context (device model, OS version, app version, coarse region derived from IP). These events never include hours, amounts of money, workplace or employer names, pay rates, or any text from a pay stub. They are not linked to your identity, and the identifier is reset if you reinstall the app or clear its data.
documents.s: 3.2 Anonymous usage statistics — Google Analytics for Firebase

documents.t: When the app crashes, a report with technical details (device model, OS version, app version, the code path that failed, and a random installation identifier) is sent so we can fix the problem. Crash reports do not contain your hours, pay, workplaces, or pay stub text.

If you buy EveryHour Pro, the transaction itself is handled by Apple or Google; we never receive your payment details. RevenueCat receives the purchase details (product identifier, purchase and renewal status, platform and device information) and a random app user identifier, so the app can tell whether Pro is active and restore it on a new phone. This identifier is not tied to your name or email.
documents.s: 3.4 Purchases and subscriptions — RevenueCat, Apple, and Google

documents.t: If you use Settings → Send feedback, the following is sent to our support database (Google Firebase) so that we can read and answer it: your message, the type of feedback, any images you attach, the email address you type (if any), the app version, your platform, and a random identifier. Only send what you are comfortable sharing — do not attach pay stubs or other personal documents. Sending feedback is entirely voluntary.

Permission Why Required? Camera To photograph a pay stub so its text can be read on your device No — you can type the figures in by hand Photo library Only if you pick an existing photo of a stub, or save an export No Location One reading, on request, to suggest the state and city for wage rules No — you can choose the place manually Notifications Local reminders (clock-out, payday, backup, pay period) No Face ID / biometrics App lock, checked by the operating system No EveryHour does not request the advertising identifier (IDFA / AAID), does not show the App Tracking Transparency prompt, does not read your contacts, calendar, or microphone, and contains no advertising SDK.
documents.s: 4. Permissions EveryHour asks for — and the ones it does not

documents.t: To make the app work — unlock what you purchased, schedule the reminders you set, and timestamp records reliably. To fix problems — crash reports and, where it matters, the diagnostic details in a feedback report you sent. To improve the app — aggregated, anonymous usage statistics telling us which features are used and where people get stuck. To answer you — only when you contact us. We do not sell your data, use it for advertising, profile you, or share it with data brokers. There are no ads in EveryHour.

Where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies, we rely on: legitimate interests for crash reporting, abuse-free operation, and anonymous product analytics (Art. 6(1)(f)); performance of a contract for delivering and restoring purchases (Art. 6(1)(b)); and consent for optional features you turn on yourself, such as sending a feedback report or granting location access (Art. 6(1)(a)), which you can withdraw at any time by stopping use of that feature or revoking the permission in system settings.

Recipient Role Data involved Google LLC / Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics, feedback database and storage, time check Usage events, crash reports, feedback content and attachments, IP address RevenueCat, Inc. Purchase / entitlement management Anonymous purchaser ID, product ID, purchase status, device and platform info Apple Inc. App Store distribution, in-app purchases, Face ID, local notifications Purchase and entitlement data Google LLC (Play) Google Play distribution and in-app purchases Purchase and entitlement data These providers process data on servers in the United States and other countries, which may be outside your country of residence. Where required, such transfers rely on the safeguards those providers offer — including the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses and, where applicable, the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Each provider processes data under its own privacy policy. We use no advertising networks, no attribution or MMP SDKs, and no analytics providers beyond the ones named above.

Data Kept for Everything in section 2 (on your device) Until you delete it in the app, use Settings → Delete all data, clear app data, or uninstall EveryHour Analytics events The retention period configured in Firebase Analytics — currently up to 14 months — then deleted or aggregated Crash reports Up to 90 days, per Crashlytics' retention Feedback reports and attached images While being handled, and for a reasonable period afterwards as a record; deleted earlier on request Purchase / entitlement data at RevenueCat For as long as needed to provide entitlement service, per RevenueCat's own retention policy Backups and exports you saved elsewhere Entirely under your control — delete them wherever you put them

Depending on where you live — including under the GDPR/UK GDPR, the CCPA/CPRA in California, and comparable laws elsewhere — you may have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict, or object to the processing of your personal information, to receive a copy of it in a portable format, to withdraw consent, and not to be discriminated against for exercising these rights. In practice, for EveryHour: Data on your device — you control it directly. Edit or delete individual records in the app, use Settings → Delete all data to erase every record, photo, note, and export at once, or uninstall the app. We hold no copy, so there is nothing for us to delete. Analytics and crash data — reinstalling the app, or clearing app data, resets the installation identifier and disconnects future data from past data. To have data associated with your current installation deleted, email us; we will need the approximate dates so we can locate it. Purchase / entitlement data at RevenueCat — email us and we will submit a deletion request on your behalf, or contact RevenueCat directly. A feedback report you sent us — email us from the address you used, or quote the report, and we will delete the report and its attachments. Write to vincenttrandeveloper@gmail.com. We aim to respond within 30 days. You may also lodge a complaint with your local data protection authority; in the EEA, that is the authority for your country of residence.

EveryHour is meant for working adults and is not directed at children under 13 (or the higher minimum age set by your local law, such as 16 in parts of the EEA). We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. The app contains no ads, no social features, and no user-to-user content. If you are a parent or guardian and believe a child has sent us personal information through the feedback form, contact us and we will delete it.

Data on your device is protected by the operating system's app sandbox and device encryption, and can be locked behind Face ID, a fingerprint, or a passcode. Backups are encrypted with a password only you hold. Data in transit is sent over HTTPS/TLS, and access to our Firebase project is restricted to the publisher. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

We may update this policy as the app changes. The "Last updated" date at the top will change, and for material changes — for example a genuinely new category of data collection — we will give notice in the app or in the release notes before the change takes effect. Continuing to use the app after a change takes effect means the updated policy applies.

EveryHour is a documentation and estimation tool. It helps you record the hours you work, compares your pay stubs against those records using the wage rules in the app's data, and prepares reports and letters from your records. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create a lawyer–client relationship. Wage laws change and have exceptions the app does not cover. For advice about your situation, contact a lawyer, a legal aid organization, or the labor agency for your state. Amounts and deadlines are estimates. They depend on the records you enter, the numbers you confirm from your pay stubs, and the wage rules in the app at the time — each report shows the version of those rules and when they were last checked. Text read from a pay stub may be inaccurate or incomplete. You are responsible for reviewing and correcting it before relying on it. The App does not file anything with an employer, agency, or court, and does not contact anyone on your behalf. We may add, change, or suspend features without advance notice where permitted by law.
documents.s: 2. What EveryHour is — and is not

documents.t: You are responsible for the accuracy of what you enter. The App keeps every change to a shift as a new entry with the reason you give, so your records show their history; please record your time honestly. Your records are stored on your phone (see the Privacy Policy). Keep your own backups — we cannot recover data that was deleted, lost with a phone, or locked inside a backup whose password you no longer have.
The App has no accounts. You do not register, and we do not issue credentials. Access to your records is controlled by your device and, if you enable it, the App's lock.

Some features require EveryHour Pro, purchased inside the App. All payments are processed by Apple or Google, charged to the account you are signed in with at confirmation of purchase. We do not process or receive your payment details.

Pro is offered as a monthly subscription, a yearly subscription, or a one-time lifetime purchase. The plans available to you, and their prices, are shown in the App before you buy. There are no free trials.

Subscriptions renew automatically for the same period unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Your account is charged for renewal within 24 hours before the period ends. You can manage or cancel a subscription at any time in your store account settings: iOS: Settings → [Your Name] → Subscriptions Android: Play Store → Profile → Payments & subscriptions → Subscriptions Deleting the App does not cancel a subscription. Cancelling stops future renewals; the current paid period runs to its end.

Prices are set per storefront and may differ by country and over time; applicable taxes are collected by Apple or Google. Where a subscription price changes, the store will seek your consent as its rules require before the change takes effect for you.
Refunds are handled by Apple or Google under their own policies. We cannot issue refunds for purchases made through the stores, but we will help you with a request where we can.
If a subscription lapses or is cancelled, Pro-only features stop being available. Your hours, pay stubs, reports, and exported files stay on your phone and remain readable.

Do not use the App: to create false records or to misrepresent hours worked; in violation of any applicable law, or of an obligation you owe to your employer or anyone else; to reverse engineer, decompile, tamper with, or circumvent the App's records, its integrity checks, or its purchase verification, except to the extent that applicable law expressly permits it.
